key_insight: PD-CogT-Sleep will test whether auditory stimulation targeting deep sleep improves cognitive training responsiveness in people with Parkinson’s disease and mild cognitive impairment.
clinical_relevance: If effective, this non-pharmacological combination could help address cognitive difficulties in Parkinson’s disease, but benefits remain unproven.
method: Single-center, double-blind, randomized sham-controlled trial targeting 50 participants.
Compare remotely delivered digital cognitive training plus phase-targeted auditory stimulation versus training plus sham stimulation.
Assess outcomes at baseline, five weeks post-allocation, and three-month follow-up.
evidence_signal: This design paper reports no efficacy results; planned assessments prioritize executive function and include other cognitive outcomes, participant reports, blood biomarkers, and sleep EEG markers.
watch_item: The small, single-center trial may limit generalizability, and exploratory biomarker changes would not establish disease modification.
paper_title: Enhancing deep sleep with auditory stimulation to boost cognitive training responsiveness in people with Parkinson's disease and mild cognitive impairment: Rationale and design of the double-blind randomized controlled trial PD-CogT-Sleep
